results.title: Hadrian Raises $1.37B Series D to Build Highly Automated Factories to Accelerate America's Industrial Renewal
excerpts:
At a time when demand for trusted U.S. manufacturing capacity continues to outpace supply, Hadrian is expanding the AI-powered production network needed to strengthen deterrence, accelerate delivery, and restore America's ability to build.

The raise values Hadrian at $7.87 billion. The financing will be co-led by WCM Investment Management, Washington Harbour Partners, Valor Equity Partners, 137 Ventures, and Baillie Gifford.

**JPMorganChase's Strategic Investment Group** joined as anchor co-lead, investing through the firm's **Security and Resiliency Initiative,** a program dedicated to strengthening the industries critical to national and economic security.

The round also included major participation by 1789 Capital, as well as participation from Morgan Stanley Wealth Management, funds managed by Apollo, accounts advised by T. Rowe Price Associates, Inc., CapitalG, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, Lux Capital, Altimeter, Construct Capital, and existing investors.
This capital will accelerate Hadrian's ability to deliver not just precision parts, but full mission-critical systems. With its "Factories-as-a-Service" model, Hadrian can rapidly scale production across munitions, shipbuilding, and other high-priority programs.

"Production is now the frontline of deterrence," said Chris Power, founder and CEO of Hadrian. "America's ability to lead will depend on whether we can build, train, and scale faster. This financing allows Hadrian to accelerate building the Factories of the Future, expand into new mission-critical production capabilities, and invest in the technicians and engineers who will rebuild America's industrial base."

Since its Series C financing just 12 months ago, Hadrian has rapidly expanded its manufacturing footprint and capabilities.

...

As Hadrian expands, it is building not only new production capacity–it is also broadening access to technician equity, giving the people building America's next generation of manufacturing capacity a direct stake in the company's success.

Together with its growing network of industrial partners, Hadrian is using its Series D to accelerate the manufacturing ecosystem required to help America build again by expanding the factories, capabilities, and workforce needed to deliver mission-critical systems at scale.

**About Hadrian  
** Hadrian is rebuilding America's industrial base with highly automated factories that combine process engineering, AI, and robotics. Its mission is to help space and defense manufacturers produce full programs at scale in the U.S. while giving American workers the tools to compete globally.

# Hadrian raises $1.37B Series D at nearly $8B to scale US defence factories

**What's the deal?** Hadrian , a factory builder and defence manufacturer, has raised $1.37 billion in a Series D round, valuing it just shy of $8 billion. JPMorgan Chase Dealroom has a profile for this one. Try Dealroom → 's Strategic Investment Group anchored as co-lead, investing through the firm's Security and Resiliency Initiative.

**Follow the money:** Backers include WCM Investment Management Dealroom has a profile for this one. Try Dealroom → , Washington Harbour Partners Dealroom has a profile for this one. Try Dealroom → , Valor Equity Partners , 137 Ventures , and Baillie Gifford . The round lands a little over a year after a $260 million Series C.
**How it works:** Hadrian produces precision parts and offers factories-as-a-service for aerospace and defence. It pairs skilled workers with AI, automation, and robotics, run through proprietary software called Opus.

**Why now?** Wars in the Middle East and Eastern Europe have pushed production capacity into the spotlight. US troops overseas are firing interceptors and missiles faster than they are being made at home, though the Pentagon has denied stockpile depletion.

**What's the endgame?** Hadrian has nearly 3 million square feet across four sites and works with the largest arms makers, including Lockheed Martin Dealroom has a profile for this one. Try Dealroom → and RTX Dealroom has a profile for this one. Try Dealroom → , as well as newer players like Anduril Industries Dealroom has a profile for this one. Try Dealroom → . In March 2026, the US Navy said the company would mass-produce submarine components in Alabama for the Virginia-class and Columbia-class programmes.
**What's next?** The company is planning a new headquarters in Los Angeles and an engineering and research-and-development hub in San Francisco.

**What they're saying:** "We were early," chief executive Chris Power Dealroom has a profile for this one. Try Dealroom → told [Axios](https://www.axios.com) . "This has been a five-year slog, and only 18 months ago everyone went, 'Oh, God, manufacturing is super important, and we really need to create new American manufacturing jobs fast.'"

**The signal:** At $1.37 billion, this ranks among the very largest US Series D rounds in machine learning, a top-percentile raise across 260 comparable deals. It marks a wager that American reindustrialisation has moved from niche cause to mainstream investment thesis. As Power puts it: "Being able to produce — and have advanced factories — is deterrence."

# Defense Startup Hadrian Valued at $7.87 Billion in New Round

Aug. 6, 2026, 1:00 PM UTC

Lizette Chapman Lizette Chapman Bloomberg News

Hadrian, a defense manufacturing startup that serves the Pentagon, Lockheed Martin Corp. and others, secured a $7.87 billion valuation in a funding round that will help the company expand its workforce.

JPMorgan Chase & Co. ’s Strategic Investment Group anchored the $1.37 billion Series D round, according to a statement Thursday. Valor Equity Partners and Baillie Gifford also participated in the financing deal, along with investors including Founders Fund, Andreessen Horowitz, and 1789 Capital, where Donald Trump Jr. is a partner.
Discussions of the round were previously reported by Bloomberg News.

**[Hadrian](https://www.hadrian.co)** , a Los Angeles, California-based developer of automated factories for aerospace and defense, raised $1.37 Billion in Series D funding, at $7.87 Billion valuation.

The round was co-led by WCM Investment Management, Washington Harbour Partners, Valor Equity Partners, 137 Ventures, and Baillie Gifford, with participation from 1789 Capital, Morgan Stanley Wealth Management, funds managed by Apollo, accounts advised by T. Rowe Price Associates, Inc., CapitalG, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, Lux Capital, Altimeter, Construct Capital, and existing investors.
The company intends to use the funds to accelerate factory expansion, scale workforce training programs, and continue investment in automation, AI-driven tooling, and real-time manufacturing intelligence.

Led by Founder and CEO Chris Power, Hadrian develops advanced manufacturing facilities designed to produce mission-critical components and full product lines through a “Factories as a Service” (FaaS) model that pairs advanced automation with software systems.

The company has already scaled high-throughput facilities to meet accelerating demand for domestic manufacturing capacity across the aerospace, defense, and critical infrastructure sectors.
